```md
- [ ] producer set for the new truth is listed
- [ ] consumer set for the new truth is listed
- [ ] projection/read-model surfaces are listed
- [ ] old truth path is removed or explicitly demoted from authority within the affected scope
- [ ] mixed-state behavior is no longer accepted as closure evidence
- [ ] tests proving mixed old/new behavior are removed or repriced
- [ ] recurring realization patterns are checked against existing library/commonization surfaces
- [ ] ticket declares library usage and names the governing library or rationale
- [ ] if the work exists in more than one build tenant, this backlog/active ticket carries only one tenant lifecycle and any sibling tenant work lives on its own suffixed ticket
- [ ] ticket wording, product wording, and proof claims are reconciled before closure
```

This ticket category is the local ticket-method enforcement surface for the
inside-out migration law defined in `SPEC_METHOD.md`.

The required field is:

- `migration_strategy`
- `library_usage`

Allowed values are:

- `inside_out_hard_break`
- `fundamental_re_adoption`

Allowed `library_usage` values are:

- `none`
- `consume`
- `extend`

If `library_usage: consume` or `library_usage: extend`, the ticket must name
the governing reusable library/commonization surface in `governing_library`.

If `library_usage: none`, the ticket must explain in `library_rationale` why:

- no existing reusable surface applies, or
- the pattern is still boundary-specific, or
- this is not yet a lawful recurrence/commonization candidate

For `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, closure is blocked while the
old authoritative interface still passes in normal execution within the
declared affected scope unless the ticket explicitly declares a retained
compatibility feature. A deterministically routed, non-overlapping Product scope
outside the declared affected scope remains governed by its own current
authority.

That means:

- the old path may not remain silently authoritative within the affected scope
- mixed old/new green tests do not count as migration completion
- any retained old path within the affected scope must be named as
  compatibility rather than current native truth
- retained compatibility must be justified in the ticket itself rather than
  inferred from surviving code
- proxy or partial implementations do not satisfy migration closure
- if a ticket was marked `completed` and later review shows checked closure
  items are false on the current tree, the ticket must be reopened or an
  explicitly linked successor ticket must be created; a false closure claim is
  a ticket-method defect, not just a code defect

An intermediate Product-slice milestone inside an open implementation-migration
ticket may be accepted under the path-relative promotion rule in
`SPEC_METHOD.md`. Its identity and acceptance criteria must derive from Product
plus every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design relation, and
retained predecessor claim; ticket wording cannot narrow that authority away.
The ticket remains active and must not claim migration closure until the
migration checklist and final closure law are satisfied.

Active ticket status does not renew the accepted slice's exhausted growth
authority. Work that only discharges already admitted removal, demotion, and
migration-closure proof obligations may continue within their existing bound
without claiming further Product progress. Further material producer or
consumer growth requires another still-live basis admitted under
`STDO-UP-013`; ticket activity alone is not that basis.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Migration Strategy Requirements
segments.text:
### Migration Strategy Requirements

If `migration_strategy: inside_out_hard_break`, the ticket must carry:

- a full best-guess interface inventory for the migrating contract family
- the ordered break sequence from deepest source truth outward
- the old seam each break intentionally severs
- the negative proof expected for each break

If `migration_strategy: fundamental_re_adoption`, the ticket must carry:

- the explicit human Product-authority selection of fundamental re-adoption
- the comparison with bounded evolution across Product value, feedback latency,
  authority risk, reversibility, total cost, and retained predecessor semantics
- the bounded abort or re-entry condition
- the sideways reference line or prior implementation boundary being treated as
  source material
- the module and interface adjudication surface
- explicit classifications for inherited modules, interfaces, carriers,
  projections, and proof surfaces

Allowed inherited-implementation classifications are:

- `carry_across`
- `redundant`
- `rewrite`

Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Recurring Realization And Library Declaration
segments.text:
### Recurring Realization And Library Declaration

Implementation migration tickets must declare whether the active boundary is:

- rebuilding a pattern locally
- consuming an existing reusable library/commonization surface
- extending that surface before the local implementation lands

This is what `library_usage` records.

The recurrence rule is:

- the second credible recurrence forces an explicit library/commonization review
- the third local rebuild is not acceptable by default

If review shows the same realization pattern already exists in two module
boundaries or tickets, a third local rebuild blocks implementation unless the
ticket does one of these:

- declares `library_usage: consume`
- declares `library_usage: extend`
- links an explicit do-not-commonize design decision in `library_rationale`

Preferred order is:

1. boundary-local cleanup
2. tenant-local reusable library/commonization surface
3. shared/common propagation only through separate design re-entry

If a reusable pattern is discovered during the active ticket, the second- and
third-recurrence rules above still apply. Outside those rules and the current
claim's applicable hard stops, the pattern is repricing input. It does not block
the bounded claim or require a follow-up ticket unless the owning authority
admits that follow-up.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Multi-Build-Tenant Review Rule
segments.text:
### Multi-Build-Tenant Review Rule

If the same work item is being processed across multiple build tenants, review
of backlog/active tickets must check that:

1. each tenant has its own suffixed ticket
2. each ticket names its `build_tenant`
3. each tenant ticket has its own proof surface and closure law
4. one tenant's green proof does not stand in for another tenant's closure
5. reopen, repricing, and successor work remain tenant-local unless the
   upstream source/product/design ticket itself must be changed

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Implementation Migration Review Disambiguation
segments.text:
### Implementation Migration Review Disambiguation

Implementation migration tickets must make the review problem concrete enough
that an implementor cannot land a rename, adapter, wrapper, or happy-path proof
and claim source-truth migration.

For a core-interface or carrier migration, the ticket should include a
`Functional Review Criteria` section. The criteria must be specific to the
ticket, but reviewers should be able to answer these generic questions:

1. Did the change replace control-flow-owned meaning with carrier-owned,
   algebra-owned, event-owned, or otherwise admitted source truth?
2. Did the change reduce or remove a semantic center, or only rename and
   relocate it behind helpers?
3. Is the new law expressed as a typed/closed carrier, contract, or transition
   family rather than an open dict, string protocol, or config-shaped surface?
4. Is the main step readable as a pure transform over admitted truth, or does it
   still contain orchestration that decides the law procedurally?
5. Are effects pushed to the edge, such as event emission, manifest
   publication, file/output publication, or operator delivery, instead of being
   mixed into source-truth interpretation?
6. Do downstream consumers pattern-match or otherwise consume the admitted
   carrier directly, or do they reconstruct truth from payloads, `.get(...)`,
   fallback defaults, raw text, or legacy files?
7. Are projections and reports derived from event/source truth, or can they
   still close independently as a second authority surface?
8. If deterministic gates, validation, or F_D-like checks exist, do they inform
   the current state without structurally blocking the lawful constructive or
   F_P-like path that the admitted contract permits?
9. If the same realization pattern already exists elsewhere, does the ticket
   explicitly consume or extend a reusable library/commonization surface rather
   than rebuilding it locally again?

Passing tests do not satisfy this section by themselves. A slice that keeps the
same semantic center alive behind typed wrappers, adapter-local policy, old
lists beside new algebra, fallback config, or rehydrated dict payloads still
fails migration review even if public behavior remains green.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Impacted Interface Review Checklist
segments.text:
### Impacted Interface Review Checklist

For a core-interface, carrier, or authoritative-contract migration, the ticket
must include an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be used
as closure evidence.

This checklist is a named walk of every live interface that can still bypass,
reinterpret, replay, or project the migrating truth path.

At minimum it should enumerate, when they exist:

- the source-carrier builder
- closure/register/projection builders
- deepest semantic kernel and adapter boundaries
- public wrappers, bootstrap, replay, ingest, resume, and query entrypoints
- prompt/report/projection/read-model surfaces
- constructor/materialization paths
- proof lanes and negative-proof fixtures

Each checklist item must state what counts as closure for that interface.

Examples:

- “`<conformance-module>::consume_projection` consumes the admitted carrier or
  projection and does not import raw helper authority”
- “`<query-module>::project_domain` exposes a read model only and does not
  silently rebuild the carrier when publication is absent”
- “`<gap-module>::build_canonical_gap` does not aggregate open payload rows into
  an independent closure decision”

Review rules:

- a checked box asserts truth on the current tree, not merely intended
  direction
- if review shows a checked interface item is false, the ticket is not
  closure-ready
- if an interface is intentionally deferred, the ticket must name the successor
  ticket or leave that item unchecked
- compatibility shims do not satisfy the checklist unless they are explicitly
  justified as retained compatibility
- for `inside_out_hard_break`, the checklist must describe the seam inventory
  before tests are used as closure evidence
- for `fundamental_re_adoption`, the checklist must cover inherited modules and
  interfaces being carried, dropped, or rewritten; implicit carry-forward does
  not count

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Required Break Order And Break-To-Closure Map
segments.text:
### Required Break Order And Break-To-Closure Map

Implementation migration tickets that touch a core interface must include a
`Required Break Order` or equivalent ordered execution section.

The order must start at the authoritative source carrier and move outward:

1. discover the full best-guess interface family
2. publish or admit the new source carrier
3. deliberately sever one old authoritative seam and keep it broken
4. rebind the deepest semantic kernel to that carrier
5. remove or demote old producers
6. rebind old consumers
7. reprice projections, reports, prompts, delivery bindings, and tests

The ticket must also include a `Break-To-Closure Map` when the migration has
multiple old interfaces. The map must state which break closes which
closure-law clause. Without that map, partial landing can look like full
landing.

Reviewers must treat the following as explicit defects:

- a typed wrapper that still carries old semantic authority
- a new carrier added beside the old authoritative read model
- a proxy or partial implementation that keeps the old interface alive behind a
  new name
- constructor, replay, ingest, resume, bootstrap, or public-wrapper paths that
  bypass admission
- a projection or test that can pass without the new carrier
- a fallback path that invents missing policy, identity, target, or closure
  truth
- a downstream proof that passes while upstream source-carrier work remains open

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Mixed-State Negative Proof
segments.text:
### Mixed-State Negative Proof

For a migration ticket, positive behavior proof is not enough.

The proof surface should include at least one negative or structural proof that
the old path can no longer satisfy the closure law. Examples include:

- the severed seam in the current break is rejected before downstream repair is
  accepted as progress
- removing the new carrier makes advancement, closure, prompt assembly, or
  projection fail closed rather than silently falling back
- a legacy payload without the admitted carrier is rejected instead of
  rehydrated into current truth
- old and new truth intentionally disagree in a fixture and the new truth wins
  or the run fails closed
- a same-name carrier, graph function, route, policy, or projection source with
  different structure fails closed instead of being accepted as equivalent
- required closure proof does not depend on undeclared local fixtures or mutable
  sibling workspaces

If the old path still works in normal execution within the declared affected
scope, or remains reachable on the claimed acceptance path, the ticket remains
open unless that path is explicitly specified as retained compatibility. A
deterministically routed, non-overlapping Product scope outside the declared
affected scope remains governed by its own current authority and does not block
the migration merely because its path still works.

For tickets with an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist`, the negative proof
must exercise the named public consumers that matter for closure. Proving that
one legacy shim is bypassed is not sufficient when the live authority path
already bypasses that shim through other helpers, loaders, or rebuild paths.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Allowed Status
segments.text:
### Allowed Status

Minimum status model:

- `backlog`
- `active`
- `completed`

Projects may add `blocked`, `cancelled`, or other explicit local states later
if needed, but the base method starts with `backlog`, `active`, and
`completed`.

These values select work-carrier state, not a second result algebra. A claim
that a state transition is valid carries its own core result and exact
predicate. `completed` is recorded only after Condition-Based Closure And
Reuse holds, including any required owner decision; lane placement cannot
make it hold. A cancelled activity does not thereby satisfy its original
delivery predicate. Where obligations were withdrawn or deferred, completed
carrier state retains those decisions and does not assert their delivery.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/Ticket Lanes
segments.text:
### Ticket Lanes

Backlog tickets live at the Product Definition Overlay's
`ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog` binding. The default is:

- `.ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/`

Active tickets live at `ticketing.tickets.lanes.active`. The default is:

- `.ai-workspace/tickets/active/`

Completed tickets move to `ticketing.tickets.lanes.completed`. The default is:

- `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/`

The intended meaning is:

- `backlog`: accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part
  of the current execution focus
- `active`: the current bounded execution set
- `completed`: closed work retained as history

This keeps the live execution set small enough that `rg` remains fast and
readable without forcing deferred work into comments or goals.

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Ticket Rules/One-Truth State Projection And Drift Refusal (`STDO-UP-009`)
segments.text:
### One-Truth State Projection And Drift Refusal (`STDO-UP-009`)

Given F2, F3 and F6, a work view cannot establish or alter an owner's current
state merely by displaying it. [Faithful projection](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#faithful-projection)
supplies that consequence. UP-009 chooses the work-carrier authority chain and
drift refusal; the listed owners retain their actual state-transition grants.

Work-carrier state has one authority chain: Goals own the bounded work wave, the ticket
owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone state, and
accepted design owns realization decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers,
indexes, and generated summaries are projections.

Apply [Faithful projection](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#faithful-projection) with
that authority chain as source, the current work-state consumer as target and
its required milestones and acceptance evidence as material dependencies.
Contradiction among those sources blocks closure; historical evidence retains
its historical standing in the view.

---

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Recommended Ticket Shape
segments.text:
## Recommended Ticket Shape

Recommended sprint shape:

```md
# SPRINT-2026-04-30 Operational Projection UX Iteration

- id: SPRINT-2026-04-30-operational-projection
- status: active
- goal: operational-projection-ux
- opened_at: 2026-04-30T09:00:00Z
- updated_at: 2026-04-30T09:00:00Z

## Authority

- specification/GOALS.md#operational-projection-ux
- specification/PRODUCT.md#operational-projection
- <governing-design-surface>/OPERATIONAL_PROJECTION.md

## Scope

Iterate an operational projection surface for layout, readability,
interaction affordance, and visual evidence quality.

## Excluded Boundaries

- no product truth changes
- no data contract changes
- no runtime or governance semantics changes
- no new constructive carrier

## Expected Change Classes

- realization_refactor

## Iterations

- id: UXI-001
  intent: improve relation-line readability
  evidence_ref: screenshots/2026-04-30/UXI-001.png
  debt: accessibility contrast check pending

## Closure

- closure_trigger: timebox, changed surface volume, or design-lead close request
- closure_law: forensic walkthrough reviews each changed state against authority
- proof_surface: screenshots plus walkthrough notes
- deferred_compliance: screenshots, accessibility check, event-replay review
- non_closure_conditions: product truth or data contract drift remains hidden
- paydown_policy: open paydown tickets for accepted local debt; reprice authority drift
```

```md
# T-001 Add Product Layer To SPEC_METHOD

- id: T-001
- type: feature
- ticket_category: ordinary
- status: active
- goal: methodology-bootstrap
- change_intent: make the product-definition layer explicit in the constitutional chain
- change_class: product_reprice
- re_entry_point: product
- triaged_at: 2026-04-07
- priority: high
- created_at: 2026-04-07
- updated_at: 2026-04-07

## Context

`SPEC_METHOD.md` included intent and requirements flow but omitted the explicit
product-definition layer.

## Acceptance

- `PRODUCT.md` is part of the constitutional chain
- bootstrap sequence includes `intent -> product -> requirements`
- examples and reconstruction logic reflect the new layer

## Links

- comment: `.ai-workspace/comments/<agent-id>/...`
```

For an implementation migration ticket:

```md
# B-010 Replace Mixed Gap Projection With One Authoritative Carrier

- id: B-010
- type: bug
- ticket_category: implementation_migration
- migration_strategy: inside_out_hard_break
- library_usage: none
- library_rationale: this migration is boundary-specific and does not establish a recurring realization pattern
- status: active
- goal: operator-gap-truth
- change_intent: replace the mixed operator gap truth with one authoritative declared carrier
- change_class: design_reframe
- re_entry_point: design_surface
- triaged_at: 2026-04-20
- created_at: 2026-04-20
- updated_at: 2026-04-20

## Migration Declaration

- affected_scope: gap projection on the declared operator-query acceptance path
- excluded_or_disjoint_scopes: none
- old_truth_path: fallback gap projection with synthetic convergence fields
- new_truth_path: explicit declared-obligation projection plus separately classified fallback gaps
- producers_old: `<gap-module>::build_fallback_gap`
- producers_new: `<obligation-module>::collect_declared_obligations`, `<gap-module>::build_canonical_gap`
- consumers_old: `<query-module>::project_gaps`, `<summary-module>::project_span`, `<review-surface>::render`
- consumers_new: `<query-module>::project_gaps`, `<summary-module>::project_span`, `<review-surface>::render`
- derived_surfaces:
  - `<query-surface>::gaps`
  - `<summary-surface>::span`
  - `<proof-surface>::first_slice_negative`
- closure_law: migration closes only when the old projection is no longer authoritative within the affected scope and mixed old/new proof does not count as acceptance

## Migration Checklist

- [ ] exact affected migration scope is named
- [ ] excluded or disjoint Product and compatibility scopes are named with deterministic routing, or explicitly declared absent
- [ ] old truth path is named explicitly
- [ ] new truth path is named explicitly
- [ ] producer set for the new truth is listed
- [ ] consumer set for the new truth is listed
- [ ] projection/read-model surfaces are listed
- [ ] old truth path is removed or explicitly demoted from authority within the affected scope
- [ ] mixed-state behavior is no longer accepted as closure evidence
- [ ] tests proving mixed old/new behavior are removed or repriced
- [ ] recurring realization patterns are checked against existing library/commonization surfaces
- [ ] ticket declares library usage and names the governing library or rationale
- [ ] if the work exists in more than one build tenant, this backlog/active ticket carries only one tenant lifecycle and any sibling tenant work lives on its own suffixed ticket
- [ ] ticket wording, product wording, and proof claims are reconciled before closure
```

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Operating Mode
segments.text:
## Operating Mode

The default local-file carrier assumes:

- humans and agents can read the active ticket folder directly
- backlog remains searchable durable work, but does not compete with the active
  lane for immediate attention
- `rg` is sufficient for finding active work
- no database or board is required

Typical commands for that default carrier:

```bash
rg -n "^#|^- status:|^- type:|^- goal:" .ai-workspace/tickets/active
rg -n "^#|^- status:|^- type:|^- goal:" .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog
rg -n "T-001|B-002" .ai-workspace/tickets
```

---

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Relationship To Other Surfaces
segments.text:
## Relationship To Other Surfaces

- `GOALS.md` answers: what broad work wave matters now
- `SPEC_METHOD.md` answers: what constitutional change class and re-entry point
  govern the work
- sprints answer: what bounded execution batch is currently pricing proof,
  evidence, and paydown
- tickets answer: what durable units of work exist and what state they are in
- comments answer: what was proposed, argued, decided, reviewed, or handed off
- `POSTING_GUIDE.md` answers: how comment-layer publications are structured and
  named

This separation prevents:

- goals becoming an overloaded backlog
- active work being diluted by every deferred ticket
- comments becoming informal task status
- task boards becoming accidental authority

---

segments.heading: Ticket Method/Future Extensions
segments.text:
## Future Extensions

This minimal method can later grow into:

- a generated active board
- ticket dependency checks
- links from tickets to scenario, requirement, or ADR surfaces
- external sync with a real ticketing system
- message-board integration through a standard tool-protocol capability

The durable local-file model remains the default and must remain valid when
selected. Another carrier is not required to reproduce its folders, but it must
preserve the same ticket authority and refusal laws.

segments.heading: Transformation Library
segments.text:
# Transformation Library

This member owns the shared transformation contracts for the
purposeful, specification-governed construction domain declared by
[Foundations](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments). Bind, Acquire, Transform,
Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose are responsibilities that can be composed or
co-located, not compulsory stages, actors or runtime APIs.

The contracts below decide recurring application, projection and composition
questions. They are conditional on the selected foundational premises and
instance choices. Particular methods bind concrete types, predicates, result
refinements, applicability, adoption and grants. Those bindings apply the
shared law; they do not restate it as a competing determination. A contract
definition grants no operation or decision authority.

Its shared contract vocabulary resolves in bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:transformation-library`, owned by the STDO Specification
Methodology Product authority. The basis is this exact member digest and its
cited source-owned contracts under the activation's governing cut; its scope
is the shared deciding contracts, conditional specialization arguments and
the explicitly imported authority vocabulary.
Named domain examples retain their source context; their role labels, types and
outcome enums are not local definitions or a shared library contract. A linked family correspondence
uses that context, while each named source function keeps its own context and
contract. Equal spelling is no equivalence or import. One function may have
several correspondences: this account is neither a partition nor a hierarchy.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Reference-only semantic imports
segments.text:
## Reference-only semantic imports

The target context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:transformation-library and its
semantic owner is the STDO Specification Methodology Product authority.
Direction is source to this contract account; meanings are unchanged owner-qualified
references, with no translation, loss, inverse or ownership transfer. The source
context and owner are declared in [Frame Method's Position](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#position).
Its exact source member digest is supplied by the selected complete cut or
frozen source inventory.
The target has its own exact member digest supplied by the frozen activation
or selected installed manifest. A review carrier is not an installed dependency
and supplies no authority. An activation binds
each member's distinct coordinates in its selected complete governing basis.
Changed member, basis,
source declaration or adoption premise invalidates reliance until applicability
is re-established. Source lifecycle and adoption conditions remain unchanged.

| Referenced concept | Source context | Exact source concept and owner |
|---|---|---|
| frame-set authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the human authority that declares or accepts the project frame set |
| semantic authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the owner of meaning for a material relation |
| evaluation authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the role permitted to perform an evaluation |
| operation authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish, or mutate a material subject where an evaluation performs such an operation |
| decision authority | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the role permitted to accept, reject, or otherwise dispose its result |
| actor identity | urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation | [Frame authority](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#authority): the human, agent, tool, or process performing work. |

These imports provide no semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority.
Missing meaning or authority bindings remain unresolved before dependent use.
The named Baseline Reviewer and WorkerResult cases below are owner-qualified
domain examples, not imported local role labels, aliases or outcome types.
Their source contracts retain applicability, adoption and activation conditions.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Foundational contract
segments.text:
## Foundational contract

Premise owner: FOUNDATIONS.md, context urn:stdo:bounded-context:foundations,
under the selected complete STDO basis. F1–F6 retain their exact definitions
at that source. Direction is source premises to the library's conditional
contracts; no meaning is translated or lost and no authority is transferred.
The target is this member's context and its Product owner declared above. The
activation or installed manifest binds both exact member digests. A changed
premise, basis or adoption condition reopens the affected argument before use.

For one selected operation, let X and Y be its declared input and output
domains, K its interpretation, P its required outcome predicate, I its material
identity/state relations and G its actual effect or decision grant. These are
parameters, not serialized fields or a universal schema. The instance owns its original domain outcomes and their total refinement into
[the core result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra). Unknown judgment,
non-performance and uncertain effects retain their separate coordinates.

- F1 and F2 require P to be about the intended subject under K; satisfying a
  different predicate cannot establish that outcome.
- F3 and F4 require I and the outer contract's material support to survive a
  handoff. Permitted variation or loss is an explicit instance choice.
- F2 requires a truthful unknown when material support is insufficient; F5
  supplies the selected domain's handling alternatives. Neither requires
  stopping unrelated authorized work.
- F6 requires an actual G before a dependent effect or disposition. Sufficient
  evidence for P cannot supply G.

An instance of Acquire returns support adequate for its selected predicate, or
the applicable core result on that exact acquisition predicate, retaining its
scope, basis or insufficient-support cause; Transform preserves the material
relations of the selected X-to-Y contract; Evaluate judges P rather than granting
effects; Conjoin uses the selected composite rule; Dispose chooses only from
already permitted actions. Bind supplies their current instance coordinates.
A single function can discharge several responsibilities. Every result uses the [core algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra); domain
refinements and independent assessment conditions stay with their owners.

The following arguments use the standing in
[Foundational commitments](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments). Their
instance premises are the selected operation, source-to-consumer relation,
composite or interrupted work named in the first column. Those instances are
not entailed by finite capacity. The linked contracts decide the questions;
the arguments identify what remains for each consumer to bind.

| Deciding contract and consumers | Premises and pillar contribution | Consequence at the decision | Additional choice and owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Contract application](#contract-application): design admission, Spec enclosing-relation admission and frame activation | F1/F2 bind the intended predicate; F3 binds its subject; F4 preserves material joins; F6 bounds effects. Specification supplies the governing constraints, functional design the typed boundary, and evidence/authority the support and grant. | A shape-correct candidate or satisfied local check is insufficient when a material governing seam or operation grant is missing. Decide admissibility on the bound relation before using it; do not treat admission as outcome success. | The domain owns its predicate, sufficiency boundary, exceptions and commit unit. This contract owns the six shared application conditions, not a new validation stage. |
| [Faithful projection](#faithful-projection): RF-017, AC-017 and domain publications | F2 requires interpreted meaning and F4 preserves the consumer's distinctions. Information and interpretation supply the source/view relation; axiomatic calculus supplies an explicit constraint representation where selected. | A consumer must recover the permission, prohibition and unresolved condition its decision needs. A structurally valid view that loses any of these cannot discharge that reliance. | The source owns meaning; the binding selects exactness or admitted approximation and required acquisition routes. Domain publication and adoption owners retain their additional conditions. |
| [Composition law](#composition-law): Design UP-016/017, Spec UP-021, AC-016 and frame joins | F4 requires typed compatibility and preserved outer obligations; F2 separates the claims being composed. Algebraic calculus supplies the composition law, functional design the joins and computational execution any effect equations. | Local validity cannot establish an unsupported material join. Result conjunction does not compose internal executions, and associativity does not establish parallel or reordered effects. | Each composite owner selects its outer predicate, join and supported forms; the execution binding proves any stronger effect equivalence. |
| [Recovery law](#recovery-law): Product continuation, ticket resumption and adopted runtime recovery | F3 supplies continuing state; F2 requires current support; F5 admits interrupted work; F6 bounds the response. Outcome-driven development supplies continuation, reference frames reacquisition and execution binding the effect observations. | Reacquire enough current state to decide the next action, retain applicable progress and expose uncertain effects. A restart or lost return does not justify replay or deletion. | Domain owners supply freshness and stronger replay rules; the actual operation grant supplies permitted observation and repair. Idempotence is an operation-specific claim. |

Bind and Acquire establish these instance coordinates; Transform performs the
granted operation; Evaluate and Conjoin return evidence on the declared
predicates; Dispose uses the existing mandate. Their distinct responsibilities
can share an implementation without sharing a subject, result or authority.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Contract application
segments.text:
## Contract application

A contract bounds an operation by its input and output domains, intended
predicate, governing constraints, material relations, evidence rule and actual
grants. Its binding names their owners and current basis. These are semantic
coordinates, not a required record format. An existing design, frame, function
or work carrier can supply them; this law requires no additional carrier or
validation stage.

The application predicate is: **this proposed operation or reliance is
admissible under this bound contract**. It differs from the predicate that the
operation achieves its intended outcome. Application uses the following
conditions once at the responsible consumer:

1. **Binding.** Identify the actual subject, intended predicate, governing
   interpretation, applicable policy and source/current-state coordinates.
   Names or equal bytes alone do not supply identity, standing or applicability.
2. **Support.** Account for the conditions and material dependencies capable
   of changing this determination. Inspect through an affected seam until its
   governing obligations are covered or evidence establishes independence of
   the far side. A task boundary, partial listing or absence of observed failure
   does not establish that independence. The domain selects its completeness
   and sufficiency criteria; the actor does not silently narrow them.
3. **Preservation.** Show that required input, output and cross-boundary
   relations hold under the declared compatibility or translation, applying
   [Preservation obligations](FOUNDATIONS.md#preservation-obligations) to the
   claimed step or composition. Retain
   identity, meaning, lifecycle, producer/evidence coordinates, constraints,
   authority and effect distinctions where material. A difference may be
   lawful; it needs the instance's admitted relation. Neither universal field
   equality nor an invented translation decides compatibility.
4. **Authority.** Apply [Judgment and authority](FOUNDATIONS.md#judgment-and-authority)
   to the actual operation or decision grant for this subject and selected
   effect. Bind any required assessment under
   [Independent assessment](FOUNDATIONS.md#independent-assessment); the domain
   supplies its additional conditions and the authority requiring them.
5. **Currentness.** Acquire observations, concurrency conditions and uncertain
   effects under [Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context),
   and apply [Change impact and evidence retention](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-retention)
   to reliance on existing evidence. A
   supported changed dependency reopens the affected determination; an
   unsupported currentness claim stays unresolved. A previously satisfied
   check can be reused on supported unchanged premises; this law does not
   require rechecking fixed graphs or every unchanged relation on every event.
6. **Result.** Apply the [core result and conjunction law](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra)
   on the actual predicates. Retain known failures, absent required coverage,
   scope/basis diagnoses, original domain outcomes, performance and effects.
   Unknown applicability is not non-applicability. A supported failure does
   not disappear because another required condition is undecided.

A consumer binds these conditions to its decision and domain exceptions rather
than copying the generic conditions into a second rule. Its dependency and
authority arguments are part of the existing decision evidence. Conditional
exceptions must be named at their owning policy; a generic application cannot
invent one. A library helper can implement several consumers, but their
subjects, required evidence and powers remain separate.

These conditions constrain what counts as admissible; they do not give a
universal algorithm for deciding arbitrary predicates. Insufficient support
returns the applicable core uncertainty or scope/basis result. A known violated
condition is retained with its evidence. A supported admissibility result
permits only the already-granted operation; it predicts neither success nor
termination. The control contract handles its observed outcome separately.

At design admission the bound instance is the proposed transition and its
complete enclosing relation. At frame activation it is the declared evaluation,
subject, basis and actor. Both use these same conditions; the design commit
predicate and frame capability predicate remain different domain decisions.
A consumer uses the supported condition once and retains its validity route;
a boundary crossing alone neither requires a second proof nor permits omission
of a changed material dependency.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Contract application/Constraint surface
segments.text:
### Constraint surface

For a current subject and basis, the bound contract describes the work allowed
by its constraints and grants. It also exposes obligations still unresolved.
This is the task's constraint surface. It distinguishes the permitted choices
inside the contract from the choices reserved to an owner. A missing condition
is not freedom; a condition proved irrelevant to this task need not be loaded
again while that proof remains applicable.

The surface can be represented as prose, typed relations, predicates, a_c or a
faithful task view. Dependencies can form a graph; they need not form a tree or
prescribe one execution order. A model must retain the distinction between
established facts, assumed premises, discretionary choices and unknowns. Its
constraint satisfaction result does not authenticate its observations or
appoint an actor. [a_c interpretation](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-017-interpretation-fidelity)
binds the source-to-model relation and its independent evidence.

Two different implementations may both lie within this surface. Selection
between them follows the declared outcome, cost and owner criteria, not a
hidden requirement for the author's preferred implementation. A worker acquires
the sufficient constraints **and the actual material subject**; the abstract
surface alone is not a complete activation.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Contract application/Faithful projection
segments.text:
### Faithful projection

A projection or interpretation applies Contract application to a declared
source-to-consumer relation. Its binding states the authoritative source and
selector, target interpretation, consumer task, required distinctions, admitted
loss or approximation, and invalidation conditions. Source and target retain
their own identities. The domain owns additional publication and adoption
conditions.

For an exact projection, a consumer must recover the same material
determinations from the view and the owning source. Approximation requires a
declared adequacy relation and evidence of its end-to-end bound; local
tolerances alone do not compose. Lost authority, a weakened condition or an
unknown promoted to permission is a fidelity defect, not compression.

The binding determines whether a full reproduction, a narrower sufficient view
or an available authentic reference is required. Omitted task-irrelevant
material can remain at its owner. Material omissions, stale sources or
unavailable references prevent the corresponding reliance; they do not require
copying every source body into every event. A view has no independent power to
change its source meaning. Its currentness is established from the selected
source and dependency state, not from its label or generation timestamp alone.

Check fidelity against independently specified source decisions: at least the
material permissible, prohibited and unresolved distinctions for the selected
claim. A self-consistent model, matching schema, checksum or generated diff
checks a different relation. Failure re-enters the first owning defect: source
ambiguity, interpretation, projection, producer or consumer. It does not license
changing the source to agree with its view.

The consuming task determines which distinctions the check must preserve.
For an RF-017 frame view these include the evaluation's failure detections and
capability conditions; for an AC-017 interpretation they include the represented
predicates, dependencies and permitted latitude. A representation adequate for
one of those claims is not evidence for the other without the corresponding
source-to-consumer binding. This is the informational consequence of F2/F4;
neither predicate decidability nor a particular serialization follows from it.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Work/recovery specialization
segments.text:
## Work/recovery specialization

This chain specializes the generic contract for interrupted, purposeful work.
It assumes an admitted work identity, persistent workspace, selected outcome,
actual grants and a material uncertain effect. These are explicit instance
premises; they do not follow from finite capacity alone.

| Premises | Conditional consequence | Particular contract and independent choice |
|---|---|---|
| F1, F2; selected outcome and current subject. Specification supplies the destination; information supplies the interpreted claim. | A current claim needs its actual predicate and support, not a remembered green status. | Spec Method UP-020 binds target truth and checkpoint; RF-005 fixes basis/coordinates. The owner chooses the outcome. |
| F2, F5; coupled material obligations and finite actor. Reference frames supply sufficient acquisition under the actor's capability. | Acquire sufficient material or return the admitted uncertainty; omitted support cannot become satisfaction. | RF-003/RF-014 bind sufficiency/capability; the work entry locates a responsibility view. Frame selection and configuration authority remain independent grants. |
| F3, F4; persistent work and affected dependencies. World models and identity supply the continuing subject; outcome-driven development supplies preservation through continuation. | Re-enter on observed current state, retaining applicable progress and reconsidering changed support. | [Computed Classification And Treatment](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment) and [Ticket reuse](TICKET_METHOD.md#work-carrier-to-execution-rule) bind applicability, invalidation and the wider frontier when dependency independence is unproved. Their concrete freshness rules are domain policy. |
| F2, F3, F6; an effect is uncertain and repetition could duplicate it. Computational execution supplies the effect boundary; evidence and authority distinguish observation from permission. | Neither historical intent nor a timeout proves completion or grants a safe repeat. Observe/reconcile, select another permitted action, or return unresolved. | [Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) owns the generic unknown-effect rule; [Computed Classification And Treatment](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment) binds its Product context. The operation grant supplies allowed observation and repair. Idempotence must be established for the actual operation. |
| F1, F4, F6; required results and current mandate. Algebraic calculus preserves the required conjunction; outcome-driven development relates continuation to the selected destination. | Preserve failures, uncovered obligations and uncertainty; choose only an already-authorized continuation or truthful stop. | UP-020, declared conjunction and any adopted Baseline engagement specialize evaluation/disposition. Independence, decision rule and role adoption are additional owner choices. |

The consequences are arguments about the stated premises, not proofs of every
source clause. Concrete work-carrier layout, number of actors, numeric budgets,
optional Baseline adoption, release procedure and all domain result enums are
independent choices. They are not inferred from the foundational commitments.
This chain leaves those choices at their owners and adds no mandatory ledger.

A recovery activation uses the sufficient projected clauses and actual subject.
It need not load this entire argument, every method or historical event bodies.
The [ordinary work entry](../plugins/spec/skills/stdo-work/SKILL.md#acquire-the-responsibility-frame)
locates that material after basis selection. Its projection does not become a
rival authority or guarantee sufficiency for a different task.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Transformation-admission specialization
segments.text:
## Transformation-admission specialization

This instance assumes a consequential entity transition, an identified current
predecessor, a declared candidate family, a durable commit boundary and actual
admission authority. These domain choices supplement F1–F6; the foundational
commitments do not choose an admission predicate, quorum or supported topology.

| Premises | Conditional consequence | Particular deciding owner and policy |
|---|---|---|
| F2, F3; current entity and predecessor are material. World models and identity contribute scoped objects and state; interpretation binds the evidence to them. | A candidate or judgment about another identity or superseded basis cannot establish this transition. | UP-016 declares exact basis continuity and enclosing joins; the domain chooses its identity and currentness law. |
| F4; a transition crosses material governing seams. Algebraic calculus supplies compatible composition; functional design carries inherited invariants across the join. | Local validity cannot establish conservation of an unexamined affected relation; omitted support remains unresolved. | UP-017 determines the affected network and inherited invariants. Domain seam declarations supply design evidence; each UP-021 admission owner still derives and validates its complete enclosing relation and any claimed far-side independence. |
| F6; proposal, judgment and durable admission are distinct. Evidence and authority supply separate support and operation grants. | A projection or satisfied judgment supplies evidence, not the missing admission grant. | UP-016 declares admitters, cardinality and competing-path disposition; UP-021 alone owns admission and standing-test semantics. |
| F2, F5; supported forms or commit effects are unresolved. Computational execution supplies the real effect boundary; outcome-driven development retains failure and recovery conditions. | Missing support cannot establish admission or non-applicability. Unknown effects remain explicit before dependent use. | UP-016 declares supported boundaries, partial-failure coverage and reconstruction; the owning admission relation retains its concrete outcomes. |

The [design admission consumer](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#admission-contract-use)
binds this contract to its transition relation and uses the consequences to
distinguish valid support from a shape-correct candidate lacking material basis
or authority. Its predicate, result refinement, commit-unit decomposition and
permitted direct/composite/nested forms remain domain policy. This application neither derives those choices nor creates an additional
validation pass. [Contract application](#contract-application) supplies the
shared decision; the design consumer binds its domain admission obligations.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Bind
segments.text:
## Bind

Recover the current purpose, subject identity, governing specification, role,
authority, state and required relations. Conflicting, missing or stale bindings
are explicit results. Apply
[Judgment and authority](FOUNDATIONS.md#judgment-and-authority) to the actual
grants and distinct authority relations for this instance.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Acquire
segments.text:
## Acquire

Apply [Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) to the
selected task. Bind the current subject, requirements, grant and destination;
resolve sufficient authentic material and material dependencies; reconcile stale
summaries with observations. That owner distinguishes context fit from attention
adequacy and states their evidence boundaries. For capacity misfit, apply [the admitted response rule](FOUNDATIONS.md#finite-capacity-and-total-handling);
the selected grant determines available refinement, reassignment or escalation.
Capacity does not license omission.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Transform
segments.text:
## Transform

Construct output or perform effects within the bound contract. Preserve the
original producer, material inputs and observed effects. Return the instance-owned outcome. A consumer-adopted, lawfully activated
[Baseline WorkerResult](STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#derived-worker-frame)
retains its declared outcomes; an [AC-013 instance](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-013-transformation)
retains that owner's outcomes. These are original domain outcomes mapped under the core result contract. Apply the unknown-effect rule at [Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context). The worker's internal search is its HOW; it cannot widen
the outer outcome or effect grant.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Evaluate
segments.text:
## Evaluate

Apply the [core result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) to the exact
predicate, subject and basis. Preserve the original domain outcome, performance,
effect observations, citations and residual coverage. A domain's evaluation
rule determines what evidence decides its predicate; it does not introduce a
parallel result algebra. Apply
[Independent assessment](FOUNDATIONS.md#independent-assessment) wherever that
rule requires it and [Judgment and authority](FOUNDATIONS.md#judgment-and-authority)
to its evaluation, operation and decision bindings. A function may exercise
decision authority already admitted by its own contract, while the
[Baseline Reviewer](STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md) retains the grant defined
by that profile.

Bind [Assertions and observations](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observations)
to the source obligation, its interpreted required predicate, the assertion's
actual target and the observation/checker basis. Establish the implication
needed by this consumer before using a local pass or failure for the broader
claim. Bind actual observation acquisition as well as the ideal checker model;
an authenticated source or execution record supplies neither missing relation.
Use [Parallel assurance and provenance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-assurance-and-provenance)
to retain the assertion's derivation and the actual execution's provenance in
the existing evidence. The result remains on its original predicate, with
unresolved fidelity, unavailable observation and non-performance distinguished.

For an UP-020 assessment, the original assessor classification is a
reason-qualified outcome on the exact cone-preservation predicate. The
[Spec disposition consumer](SPEC_METHOD.md#proportional-disposition) owns its
mapping and conditions. The actor with bound decision authority separately
returns the authorised disposition; the library supplies no second table.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Conjoin
segments.text:
## Conjoin

Apply [Result conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction) to the selected
composite predicate, required coverage and material joins. Authenticate each
contribution and retain its predicate, original outcome and supporting evidence.
Known failure and required uncovered coverage both survive the aggregate. A
planned but absent judgment is not confused with uncovered coverage outside an
authenticated plan. Another declared logical operator uses the same core result
record on its own predicate; it cannot silently weaken conjunction.

When comparison or repeated evidence is used for mutual assurance, apply
[Parallel assurance and provenance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-assurance-and-provenance)
to the material shared causes and dependencies, and
[Risk and assurance selection](FOUNDATIONS.md#risk-and-assurance-selection)
to any quantitative confidence claim. This evidence binding supplies no new
logical conjunction rule. One execution supporting several predicates is not
several independent observations.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Dispose
segments.text:
## Dispose

Apply [Judgment and authority](FOUNDATIONS.md#judgment-and-authority) to the
current decision mandate and exact subject. The actor carrying that authority
consumes the closed work and evaluation results, then selects only a disposition
the mandate permits. The decision is distinct from the assessment it consumes
and returns its own predicate-bound core result under
[Result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra).

For an agentic construction instance it selects accept, local_repair, re_enter
or reject for the declared cone under [UP-020](SPEC_METHOD.md#agentic-construction-execution-stdo-up-020). It may select a next already-authorized action or stop under the instance's
permitted outcomes. Domain-specific yield remains with its declared owner. It cannot change upstream meaning or take a reserved owner decision.
Accept binds an exact checkpoint; it does not imply release. A Product-outcome
acceptance interval is separately governed by
[UP-013](SPEC_METHOD.md#product-outcome-conservation-stdo-up-013).

Other instances retain their original domain classifications. Their owners
distinguish recorded state, evaluation outcomes and decision dispositions, and
bind each evaluation or decision to its exact core-result predicate. A recorded
status alone is neither a judgment nor an operation grant.
[Ticket Method](TICKET_METHOD.md) owns sprint/paydown and work-carrier closure
classifications; [Release Method](RELEASE_METHOD.md#successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
owns conserved/superseded/intentionally removed/not applicable. An actor carrying
that contract's bound operation authority may record condition-based closure
when that owning contract permits it.
Sharing Dispose machinery changes none of those grants or classifications.

The [UP-020 disposition conditions](SPEC_METHOD.md#proportional-disposition)
determine accept, local repair, re-entry and rejection for that contract. They
are applied once at that owner; this library does not redefine them.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Composition law
segments.text:
## Composition law

For T: X → Y and S: Y → Z, apply [Contract application](#contract-application)
to the declared outer predicate and every material join. The binding specifies
which outputs satisfy which preconditions, what each step may effect, and the
relations the composite must preserve. Local correctness is insufficient when
the join is unsupported. Distinct bases may compose under an admitted coherent
topology; distinct authorities remain distinct.

Apply [Preservation obligations](FOUNDATIONS.md#preservation-obligations) to
the instance's boundary properties, governing assumptions, transition relations
and outer outcome. Bind the initial support, step evidence, material joins and
final implication used by this particular composition; separately support the
actual execution's conformance and any claimed branch, concurrent or external
effect law. An unresolved outer argument retains its supported local results.
Refinement and approximate composition use that same owner's declared
preservation and end-to-end adequacy conditions.

[Design UP-016](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#transformation-admission-completeness-stdo-up-016)
and [UP-017](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#bounded-frame-conservation-stdo-up-017)
bind design declarations; [Spec UP-021](SPEC_METHOD.md#complete-enclosing-relation-admission-stdo-up-021)
binds complete-transition admission and its semantic commit boundary.
[Frame Method](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#using-frames-in-conjunction) binds
frame relations; [AC-016](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-016-typed-composition)
binds typed calculus paths. Their extra policies remain part of the composite
contract, rather than becoming generic rules for every composition.

Combining evaluation results applies [result conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction)
or the explicitly declared alternative operator. Combining effects preserves
their actual boundary and observations. Regrouping, reordering and concurrent
execution are different claims: associativity alone licenses neither reordered
effects nor parallel execution. The selected computational binding supplies
any additional independence or effect equations it relies on.

Categorical claims apply the complete demonstration standard in
[Orthogonal descriptions](FOUNDATIONS.md#orthogonal-descriptions). A
contract-preserving construction does not by itself establish such a claim.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Recovery law
segments.text:
## Recovery law

Apply [Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) before
selecting the next dependent action. Bind current work identity, observe changed
material state, retain applicable work and reconsider affected support. Unknown
effects stay unknown until sufficiently observed or reconciled. Private context
is replaceable; the workspace survives the actor.

[Bounded construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#bounded-construction) supplies progress,
stop and total-handling distinctions. Spec Method binds Product progress and
owning-layer re-entry; [Ticket Method](TICKET_METHOD.md#work-carrier-to-execution-rule) binds carrier use; adopted profiles bind
their additional recovery duties. Retry applies the causal-change condition in
[Bounded construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#bounded-construction). A process restart by itself is an acquisition event, not proof that a
construction restart or workspace deletion is required.

Bind [Change impact and evidence retention](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-retention)
to the observed change, assertion justification and material execution/evidence
dependencies. Use its retention relation before relying on historical support;
keep the old subject and the new applicability relation. Unknown impact, newly
required cases and mandatory gates remain part of the recovery assessment.
Selection supplies no new execution result, and recovery preserves known failures
and unresolved coverage alongside valid work.

Select assurance for the affected relation from applicable retained evidence
and required new assessment. A selected proof must be adequate to falsify that
relation and satisfy its required independence. Its cost selection follows
[UP-014](SPEC_METHOD.md#proportional-method-and-delivery-stdo-up-014) within
[Risk and assurance selection](FOUNDATIONS.md#risk-and-assurance-selection),
including the relevant acquisition, impact-analysis and assessment costs.
For a claim of continuity independent of private actor state, exclude that state
and compare the reconstructed decision with current material reality. A
same-context exercise cannot establish that claim.

segments.heading: Transformation Library/Cost and contraction
segments.text:
## Cost and contraction

[Method proportionality](SPEC_METHOD.md#proportional-method-and-delivery-stdo-up-014)
owns the justification of method burden; apply its deciding definition rather
than treating raw counts as proof of improvement. For a computational or handoff cost claim, select those
measures material to that claim. Possible measures include transferred/acquired
bytes, attention, I/O, CPU, addressable memory, critical-path elapsed time,
aggregate work or displaced human assurance. This is an illustrative choice,
not an all-fields obligation, universal quota or separate accounting carrier.

A reference reduces storage only when its resolution preserves adequacy. A
smaller document or faster local preparation does not prove whole-path
improvement. Contract duplicated meaning and authority only while preserving
required distinctions and independent evaluations.

segments.heading: The `a_c` Traversal Occurrence Profile over Mutable Subjects
segments.text:
# The `a_c` Traversal Occurrence Profile over Mutable Subjects

<!-- STDO3_PROFILE_BINDING_START -->

segments.heading: The `a_c` Traversal Occurrence Profile over Mutable Subjects/Governing Relations
segments.text:
## Governing Relations

This optional profile binds
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) to
immutable histories over an externally mutable subject. Its admission, effect
readiness and frontier-projection consumers below supply the exact record
families, predicates, equality relations, grants and result refinements.

The adopted policies are the closed signature, append-only occurrence/event
history and atomic semantic-admission cut. The exact calculus basis, profile
signature and Product adoption retain separate identities. Their finite
reference domains, cardinalities, enums, inherited records, refusal mappings
and publication-resolution conditions remain the concrete application contract.

[Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) governs current
observation and uncertain effects; the profile adds its bounded observations,
currentness law and immutable history. It supplies no scheduler, state store,
rollback mechanism or grant. Subject binding, traversal application, operation
kind, operation, executor, actor and invocation are distinct coordinates.
Reapplication preserves the evolving subject and admitted prior history without
assuming side-effect idempotence. Semantic atomicity prescribes no storage
transaction.

Within adoption, [F1–F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments) apply to
three instance conditions: the Product selects one exact calculus basis;
the subject can change outside its model while retaining a stable binding;
and each effect is a separately identified operation under an owner-issued
grant. The profile supplies finite record and history policies for those
conditions; neither calculus availability nor a recorded occurrence adopts them.

| Determination and consuming law | Conditional argument | Additional profile choice and owner |
|---|---|---|
| Closed model and adoption: [imported basis](#imported-calculus-boundary), [signature](#closed-semantic-object-sorts), [authority and adoption](#authority-and-adoption) | Axiomatic representation requires records to retain their chosen calculus meaning and exact basis (F2/F3); authority remains with its owner (F6). Thus an occurrence model uses the selected calculus populations and cannot infer an operation grant or Product vocabulary from matching names. | This profile closes its sorts, reference domains, event/relation kinds and qualifiers. The Product declares its interpretation, concrete authorities and compatible signature; absent or incomplete adoption leaves the profile inactive. |
| Occurrence identity and correction: [occurrence identity](#occurrence-identity), [OP-003](#op-003-correction-without-erasure), [OP-006](#op-006-immutable-iteration-history) | Identity distinguishes an application on exact inputs from a later reapplication (F3); evidence and correction retain what each application established (F6). Changing the current subject cannot make an earlier occurrence describe the new state or erase the evidence being corrected. | This profile chooses immutable occurrences/events and append-only correction. A new application mints a new occurrence; the Product supplies subject interpretation and correction authority. Those choices imply neither effect idempotence nor rollback. |
| Causality and precedence: [OP-001](#op-001-seed-acyclicity), [typed lineage](#causality-and-typed-lineage), [OP-004](#op-004-precedence-is-not-authority) | Information and typed composition require the kind of a relation to determine its meaning (F2/F4). Ordering facts therefore cannot establish causal or admission authority (F6). A support/correction cycle in the untyped union does not prove a cycle in one declared causal graph. | This profile chooses separate identity and causal DAGs. The Product owns admitted causal claims and its explicit precedence law; neither timestamps nor common actors supply those relations. |
| Semantic-cut admission: [admission tuple](#candidate-judgment-event-and-relation-separation), [OP-002](#op-002-atomic-semantic-admission) | Algebraic composition requires all material joins as well as component results (F4), and evidence/admission authority remain distinct (F2/F6). `j_c` and `j_e` can support `j_a`; `j_a` cannot authenticate its own input. Individual admitted records therefore do not establish a cut whose frontier, relation or basis joins fail. | This profile chooses the seven-member cut, three admitted judgments and whole-unit admission. Its exact equality and membership conditions bind core conjunction; semantic atomicity prescribes no storage transaction. |
| Effect readiness and observation: [effect relation](#mutable-subject-effect-relation), [OP-005](#op-005-mutable-reality-conservation) | Computational execution binding separates traversal kind, operation, actor and executor; identity/current state and authority bind the actual invocation (F3/F6). Finite observation permits unknown completion (F5). A readiness judgment can authorize dispatch without proving its later effect, and unauthorized mutation remains an observed effect. | This profile chooses `SubjectBinding`, exact grant joins, pre/post observations and the closed disposition/readiness relations. Product-owned containment may replace territory equality only as declared. Shared currentness and effect law decide dependent repetition; the profile supplies no lock, rollback or scheduler. |
| Frontier and projection: [frontier](#event-frontier-and-projection), [OP-007](#op-007-scope-conservation) | Information-preserving projection needs its exact source membership and interpretation (F2/F3/F4). A later event therefore changes the frontier to which a current claim refers; a latest-only summary cannot establish completeness, and a subject-wide fact cannot acquire occurrence scope for convenience. | This profile chooses immutable `EventFrontier` and projection identities with explicit precedence, boundaries and residuals. The Product supplies event-scope and projection laws; the shared faithful-projection contract evaluates that exact relation. |

<!-- STDO3_PROFILE_BINDING_END -->

segments.heading: The `a_c` Traversal Occurrence Profile over Mutable Subjects/Position
segments.text:
## Position

The **Traversal Occurrence Profile** defines an application-neutral
model-family signature for immutable application histories over an externally
mutable subject.

Its stable concept identity is:

```text
urn:stdo:concept:traversal-occurrence-profile
```

This standard owns that concept in bounded context:

```text
urn:stdo:bounded-context:traversal-occurrence-profile
```

Adoption of the profile is optional. The profile imports one exact `a_c` basis
and instantiates one closed model-family signature under its record and model
laws. It does not amend `a_c`, become part of every `a_c` model, or define a
universal execution theory.

Availability is not adoption. A Product that adopts the profile owns its
subject interpretation, concrete vocabulary, authorities, requirements,
design, implementation, and evidence. This standard imports none of those
consumer identities.

segments.heading: The `a_c` Traversal Occurrence Profile over Mutable Subjects/Scope
The `a_c` Traversal Occurrence Profile over Mutable Subjects/Imported Calculus Boundary
segments.text:
## Imported Calculus Boundary

For exact `AxiomaticCalculusBasis` identity `b_ac`, this profile declares:

```text
Sigma_occurrence = instantiate_signature(b_ac, OccurrenceSignatureDefinition)
```

`OccurrenceSignatureDefinition` imports the exact finite `RecordKind_ac` set
unchanged and declares the complete finite sets of closed sorts, relation
kinds, constraint kinds, judgment kinds, residual kinds, stop kinds, auxiliary
value domains, field reference domains, and exact inherited functor-kind refs
below. A conflicting calculus basis, inherited field meaning, record shape,
population, value domain, reference domain, relation domain, authority
coordinate, or refusal law makes instantiation invalid.

An occurrence model remains an ordinary `a_c` model:

```text
M_occ,b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J)
M_occ,b satisfies a_c[Sigma_occurrence]

Population_M_occ = {
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:semantic-object -> O,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:typed-relation -> E,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:constraint -> C,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:latitude -> L,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:residual -> X,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:traversal -> V,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:transformation -> T,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:judgment -> J
}
```

Only profile semantic objects use `SemanticObject.value`. Relations,
constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations, and judgments
retain their exact inherited `a_c` record families and coordinates.

`Population_M_occ` is total over and exactly equal to `RecordKind_ac`. Every
fundamental record occurs in exactly one finite population, local identities
are unique across the disjoint union, and every other member of `I` resolves
once through a profile-declared external reference domain and basis relation.
The profile adds sorts and value domains, never another fundamental record
kind. Its `RefDomain_Sigma_occurrence(record_kind, qualified_field)` closes
every identity-bearing value field and inherited record field to an exact
local record kind and semantic-object sort or one declared external target
kind. `qualified_field` includes the source sort or kind and complete nested
field path; nominally equal field labels never merge their domains.
Missing populations, hidden records, locally-and-externally ambiguous refs,
unknown record kinds, and undeclared field domains refuse model validation.

| `TraversalApplication` | `traversal_ref`, `functor_kind_ref`, `input_refs`, `application_contract_ref` |
| `Occurrence` | `application_ref`, `traversal_ref`, `functor_kind_ref`, `subject_binding_ref`, `intended_outcome_ref`, `lineage_refs`, `identity_dependency_refs` |
| `SubjectBinding` | `subject_ref`, `authority_ref`, `invalidation_ref`; no mutable content digest |
| `Observation` | `subject_binding_ref`, `observation_kind`, `observer_ref`, `evidence_ref`, `evidence_sha256`, `observation_coordinate_ref` |
| `IntendedOutcome` | `outcome_ref`, `outcome_contract_ref`, `comparison_basis_ref` |

| `EffectInvocation` | `occurrence_ref`, `operation_ref`, `executor_ref`, `actor_ref`, `operation_grant_ref`, `effect_territory_ref`, `input_refs` |
| `EffectDisposition` | `invocation_ref_or_none`, `disposition`, `post_observation_ref_or_none`, `effect_evidence_refs`, `residual_ref_or_none` |
| `EffectEvidence` | `invocation_ref`, `evidence_kind`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_sha256_refs`, `observation_limit_ref` |
| `RelationClaim` | `relation_kind_ref`, `source_ref`, `target_ref`, `relation_qualifiers`, `claimant_ref`, `claim_basis_ref`, `source_frontier_ref` |
| `FrameworkEvent` | `event_kind_ref`, `payload_ref`, `payload_sha256`, `scope_class`, `occurrence_ref_or_none`, `claim_ref_or_none`, `claim_judgment_ref_or_none`, `source_frontier_ref` |
| `EventFrontier` | `event_set_identity`, `member_event_refs`, `projection_basis_ref`, `precedence_law_ref` |
| `Projection` | `frontier_ref`, `projection_rule_ref`, `selected_relation_refs`, `boundary_refs`, `residual_refs` |
| `SemanticAdmissionCut` | `claim_ref`, `claim_judgment_ref`, `event_ref`, `event_judgment_ref`, `materialized_relation_ref`, `source_frontier_ref`, `successor_frontier_ref` |
| `EffectSubject` | `occurrence_ref`, `subject_binding_ref`, `pre_observation_ref`, `invocation_ref`, `operation_ref`, `operation_grant_ref`, `effect_territory_ref`, `currentness_invalidation_ref` |

Every row is a `SemanticObject` and therefore also carries exact `id`, `sort`,
`context`, `owner`, `scope`, and `basis`. The value contract is closed. An
unknown field or missing required field refuses structural admission.

`FrameworkEvent.value.occurrence_ref_or_none` is optional. An event whose
declared scope is independent of an occurrence is not assigned a fictional
occurrence to satisfy a total relation.

`claim_ref_or_none` and `claim_judgment_ref_or_none` are either both absent or
both exact. A claim-admission event requires both and a current
`source_frontier_ref`; another event kind refuses those fields unless its
compatible extension explicitly declares them.

The profile uses exact scoped identity refs, SHA-256 content digests, and
duplicate-free ordered identity-ref lists. `observation_kind` is one of
`pre_effect`, `post_effect`, or
`external_observation`. `EffectDisposition.value.disposition` is one of
`no_effect`, `completed_effect`, `partial_effect`, or `refused_effect`.
`scope_class` is one of `occurrence_scoped`, `subject_scoped`, or
`authority_scoped`. Another value requires a separately identified compatible
signature extension.
Every `_ref` resolves exactly once under AC-003. Every ref list is ordered by
the owning signature's declared order and rejects duplicates.

`TraversalApplication`, `OperationKind`, and `EffectOperation` are identity
records, not executors. An adopting Product declares its finite
`OperationKind` object population through its exact compatible signature and
mapping. The core profile declares the sort and closed record shape but no
consumer operation-kind instances. A model containing an `EffectOperation`
without an exact in-model `OperationKind` object or explicit compatible import
refuses.
